16-1.title: The Beginnings of Christianity
16-1.learn:
KEY IDEAS — THE BEGINNINGS OF CHRISTIANITY

Christianity began in the Roman lands of JUDEA (part of the eastern Roman Empire), a region where many Jewish people lived. Christianity grew out of Judaism and shared the belief in ONE God (monotheism). It taught people to follow the life and teachings of JESUS, whose followers believed he was the son of God. Jesus taught messages of love, forgiveness, kindness, and treating others well.

At first, Christianity was a SMALL group of followers. But the religion spread steadily over time. Jesus's followers, including teachers like the apostle Paul, traveled to share his teachings with new people.

Interestingly, the Roman Empire itself helped Christianity spread. The Romans had built a huge network of well-made ROADS and made TRAVEL and TRADE across the empire safe and easy (especially during the Pax Romana). These roads and trade routes let the new ideas of Christianity travel QUICKLY from place to place across the empire. So a religion that began small in one corner of the empire was able to spread widely, partly thanks to Roman roads. Remember: Christianity began in Judea, grew from Judaism, and spread along Roman roads.

questions.explanation: Christianity began in the Roman lands of Judea.

questions.question: What does the word 'monotheism' mean?

questions.question: Judea was located in which part of the Roman Empire?

questions.question: Followers of Jesus believed he was the son of whom?

questions.question: Which religion did Christianity grow OUT of?

questions.question: Which word best describes Christianity at its very beginning?

questions.question: Which pair correctly matches a place with what happened there?

questions.question: Which person is known as a teacher who helped spread early Christianity?

questions.question: Which statement BEST summarizes the lesson?

questions.question: A merchant travels a Roman trade route and hears about Jesus from another traveler. This shows that trade routes did what?

16-2.title: Christianity Spreads Through the Empire
16-2.learn:
KEY IDEAS — CHRISTIANITY SPREADS THROUGH THE EMPIRE

At first, the Roman government saw Christianity as a threat because Christians refused to worship the Roman gods or the emperor. As a result, Christians faced times of PERSECUTION, meaning they were treated cruelly and sometimes punished for their beliefs.

Even so, Christianity kept GROWING. Its messages of hope, equality, and the promise of an afterlife appealed to many people, especially the poor and the powerless. The number of Christians steadily increased across the empire.

A huge turning point came with the Roman Emperor CONSTANTINE. In the early 300s AD, Constantine made Christianity LEGAL in the Roman Empire (through the Edict of Milan), ending the official persecution. Constantine himself supported Christianity, and it spread to millions of people. Later, Christianity even became the main, official religion of the Roman Empire.

This change RESHAPED the culture and beliefs of the ancient world. A faith that had started small and persecuted became one of the most powerful and widespread religions in history. Remember: Christians were first persecuted; Emperor Constantine made Christianity legal.

questions.question: How did the Roman government FIRST treat Christians?
questions.explanation: Christians first faced persecution from Rome.

questions.question: What does 'persecution' mean?

choices.B: Being treated cruelly for one's beliefs

questions.explanation: Persecution means being treated cruelly for beliefs.

questions.question: Which emperor made Christianity legal in the Roman Empire?
questions.explanation: Emperor Constantine made Christianity legal.

questions.question: Why did the Roman government first see Christianity as a threat?

choices.A: Christians refused to worship the Roman gods or the emperor

questions.explanation: Christians' refusal to worship Roman gods worried the government.

questions.question: Despite persecution, what did Christianity keep doing?
questions.explanation: Christianity kept growing despite persecution.

questions.question: To whom did Christianity's messages especially appeal?
questions.explanation: Its message of hope appealed especially to the poor and powerless.

questions.question: After being made legal, what eventually happened to Christianity in Rome?

choices.A: It became the main, official religion of the empire

questions.explanation: Christianity later became Rome's official religion.

questions.question: What was the big effect of Christianity's spread?

choices.B: It had no effect on anyone
choices.C: It reshaped the culture and beliefs of the ancient world

questions.explanation: Christianity's spread reshaped ancient culture and beliefs.

questions.question: Which BEST describes Christianity's journey in the Roman Empire?

choices.A: It started as the official religion and shrank
choices.B: It went from small and persecuted to powerful and widespread
choices.C: It was always banned and never spread

questions.explanation: Christianity grew from a small, persecuted faith into a powerful religion.

questions.question: Constantine making Christianity legal was important because it did what?

choices.B: It ended official persecution and helped the faith spread
choices.C: It had no effect on Christians
choices.D: It made everyone worship Roman gods

questions.explanation: Legalizing Christianity ended persecution and helped it spread.

questions.question: What was the name of the law by which Constantine made Christianity legal?
questions.explanation: Constantine made Christianity legal through the Edict of Milan.

questions.question: In about what time period did Constantine make Christianity legal?
questions.explanation: Constantine made Christianity legal in the early 300s AD.

questions.question: Which ideas in Christianity's message especially gave people hope?

choices.C: Equality and the promise of an afterlife

questions.explanation: Christianity's message of hope, equality, and an afterlife appealed to many people.

questions.question: Which of the following did NOT happen to Christianity in the Roman Empire?

choices.B: It was made legal by Constantine
choices.C: It later became the official religion
choices.D: It was completely destroyed and forgotten

questions.explanation: Christianity was not destroyed; it grew and became Rome's official religion.

questions.question: What did Constantine's support of Christianity allow the religion to do?
questions.explanation: With Constantine's support, Christianity spread to millions of people.

questions.question: Christians were persecuted mainly because they refused to do what?

choices.A: Worship the Roman gods or the emperor

questions.explanation: Christians refused to worship the Roman gods or the emperor.

questions.question: Put these events in the correct order.

choices.A: Constantine legalized it, then Christians were first persecuted
choices.B: Christians were first persecuted, then Constantine made Christianity legal
choices.C: Christianity was the official religion, then it began
choices.D: Christianity was banned, then it was never heard of again

questions.explanation: First Christians were persecuted, then Constantine made Christianity legal.

questions.question: What does it mean that Christianity became the 'official' religion of Rome?

choices.A: It was the main religion supported by the empire
choices.B: It was banned by the empire
choices.C: It was practiced only in secret
choices.D: It was the smallest religion in Rome

questions.explanation: Being the official religion meant it was the main religion supported by the empire.

questions.question: Why was Constantine's decision a 'turning point' for Christianity?

choices.C: It ended official persecution and let the faith grow freely
choices.D: It forced everyone to worship Roman gods

questions.explanation: Constantine's decision ended official persecution and let the faith grow freely.

questions.question: Which of these is the BEST example of persecution?

choices.D: Christians being punished for their beliefs

questions.explanation: Being punished for one's beliefs is an example of persecution.

questions.question: Imagine a poor person in the Roman Empire. Why might Christianity's message appeal to them?

choices.A: It promised them an army to command
choices.B: It offered hope, equality, and a promise of an afterlife
choices.C: It made them a Roman emperor
choices.D: It gave them a palace right away

questions.explanation: Christianity offered hope, equality, and the promise of an afterlife, which appealed to the poor.

questions.question: Which statement compares Christianity BEFORE and AFTER Constantine?

choices.A: Before, it was official; after, it was banned
choices.B: Before and after, it was always illegal
choices.C: Before, it was persecuted; after, it was legal and growing
choices.D: It never changed in any way

questions.explanation: Before Constantine, Christianity was persecuted; after, it was legal and growing.

questions.question: What happened to the number of Christians across the empire over time?

choices.D: It was always larger than the whole empire

questions.explanation: The number of Christians steadily increased across the empire.

questions.question: The spread of Christianity 'reshaped' the ancient world. What does 'reshaped' mean here?
questions.explanation: 'Reshaped' means it changed the culture and beliefs of the ancient world.

questions.question: Which best describes a Christian during the time of persecution?

choices.A: Someone rewarded by Rome for their faith
choices.B: Someone who could be punished for their beliefs
choices.D: Someone who worshiped many Roman gods

questions.explanation: During persecution, a Christian could be punished for their beliefs.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a reason Christianity appealed to many people?

choices.D: It promised great wealth and an army

questions.explanation: Christianity appealed through hope, equality, and an afterlife, not wealth and armies.

questions.question: What does the word 'legal' mean when we say Constantine made Christianity legal?
questions.explanation: 'Legal' means allowed by law.

questions.question: If a religion is 'persecuted' but still 'keeps growing,' what does that show?

choices.B: That punishment instantly stopped all believers
choices.C: That its message was strong enough to attract people despite hardship
choices.D: That no one ever believed in it

questions.explanation: Growing despite persecution shows the message was strong enough to attract people despite hardship.

questions.question: Which emperor is remembered for supporting Christianity and helping it spread?
questions.explanation: Constantine supported Christianity and helped it spread.

questions.question: Which sentence shows cause and effect correctly?

choices.A: Christians worshiped Roman gods, SO they were persecuted
choices.B: Constantine banned Christianity, SO it became legal
choices.C: Christianity shrank, SO it became the official religion
choices.D: Christians refused to worship Roman gods, SO the government saw them as a threat

questions.explanation: Because Christians refused to worship Roman gods, the government saw them as a threat.

questions.question: Before Constantine, how did the Roman government view Christianity?

choices.C: As a harmless hobby it encouraged
choices.D: As a branch of Roman law

questions.explanation: Before Constantine, the Roman government saw Christianity as a threat.

questions.question: Which is the BEST summary of how Christianity changed in Rome?

choices.A: It began as the official religion and was then banned
choices.B: It stayed small and persecuted the entire time
choices.C: It went from persecuted to legal to the official religion
choices.D: It was created by Constantine from nothing

questions.explanation: Christianity went from persecuted, to legal, to the official religion of Rome.

questions.question: What does 'afterlife' mean in Christianity's message of hope?
questions.explanation: 'Afterlife' means a life after death, part of Christianity's message of hope.

questions.question: A historian says Christianity became 'one of the most powerful and widespread religions in history.' What does this describe?

choices.D: Its huge growth and influence over time

questions.explanation: This describes Christianity's huge growth and influence over time.

questions.question: Which statement is TRUE about Christianity after Constantine?
questions.explanation: After Constantine, official persecution of Christianity had ended.

questions.question: Which group did Christianity's promise of equality most likely comfort?
questions.explanation: Christianity's promise of equality comforted the poor and powerless.

questions.question: Why did Christianity NOT die out during the years of persecution?

choices.A: Rome paid people to join it
choices.B: There was no persecution at all
choices.D: Its message of hope kept attracting new believers

questions.explanation: Its message of hope kept attracting new believers, so it did not die out.

questions.question: Which event came LAST in Christianity's story in Rome?

choices.B: Christianity became the official religion of the empire

questions.explanation: Becoming the official religion of the empire came last in this sequence.

questions.question: Which best describes how the Roman government's view of Christianity changed?

choices.A: It went from seeing it as a threat to supporting it
choices.C: It always wanted to destroy Christianity and never stopped
choices.D: It never had any opinion about Christianity

questions.explanation: The Roman government changed from seeing Christianity as a threat to supporting it.

questions.question: Which sentence BEST captures the main idea of this lesson?

choices.A: Christianity was always the official religion and never changed
choices.B: Christianity stayed small and was never legalized
choices.C: Christians were first persecuted, then Constantine made Christianity legal and it spread widely
choices.D: Constantine destroyed Christianity in the early 300s AD

questions.explanation: Christians were first persecuted, then Constantine made Christianity legal and it spread widely.
